newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Deve Gowda wins crucial parliament vote.
newsitem.headline: India's Deve Gowda wins crucial parliament vote.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda won a crucial vote in parliament on Tuesday when his reluctant Congress party ally backed the government's policies spelled out by President Shankar Daya Sharma last month.

The "motion of thanks to the president's address", which amounts to a vote of confidence, was decided with a voice vote in the lower house of parliament, signalling the first major victory for Deve Gowda in the ongoing budget session, news agencies said.
Deve Gowda's United Front alliance controls fewer than 200 seats in the 545-member Lok Sabha, the lower house of parliament, but it has the support of the Congress party's 140 deputies.

Politicians said the government still had to watch out for potential hazards during the discussion on the budget for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March), which was unveiled on February 28 by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram.

The rightwing Hindu nationalist Bharartiya Janata Party (BJP), the single largest group in parliament, last month backed off from its proposal to move a no-confidence motion against the nine-month old government.
BJP leaders say they could still move the motion during the budget session which ends on May 12.
